title: Customer-Initiated Key Rotation & Emergency Access Proofing — Acceptance Checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define acceptance criteria and an evidence checklist for customer-initiated KMS/HSM rotations and emergency operator access flows in Private deployments. This ticket scopes the requirements for (a) customer-initiated key rotation workflows, (b) operator emergency access (break-glass) procedures, and (c) audit evidence and test scenarios required for sign-off. The goal is to produce a reproducible, testable playbook that the Security, Ops, and Customer Onboarding teams can use to validate customer deployments and that can be attached to onboarding artifacts.

Background: Customers in regulated industries require the ability to rotate keys they manage on-demand, plus documented emergency access procedures when operator intervention is necessary. Past onboarding incidents (see incident-2025-04-kms-rotation) revealed ambiguity around who must be notified, what audit events are required, and how operator access is scoped and time-limited. This PRD clarifies responsibilities and defines concrete acceptance tests.

Scope: Applies to Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) installations where customers use either: 1) customer-managed KMS (cloud provider KMS with customer keys) or 2) HSM-backed rotation flows mediated by our operator tooling. Out of scope: Hosted API rotations for Redwood-managed keys, which are handled by Platform Key Ops under a different runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Customer-initiated rotation API exists and accepts signed rotation requests: testable via demo tenant with keys scoped to test-app-rot-01
Rotation pipeline performs: artifact version check, KV cache invalidation for active sessions, controlled re-encryption of persisted secrets, and health-checked rollout to replicas within SLA
Operator emergency access flow enforces multi-party approval (2-of-3) and issues time-bound ephemeral credentials with automatic revocation at TTL expiry
All rotation and emergency access events are emitted to audit logs with required fields: actor, requester_id, key_id, action, timestamp, correlation_id, pre/post key metadata hashes
Audit logs are delivered to customer-configured destinations (S3/GCS/Event Hub) and verified for immutability within retention window during test
Playbook includes rollback steps: rekey-to-prev-version, KV cache reconciliation, and application token refresh guidance — validated in dry-run with zero data loss
Confluence playbook contains step-by-step test scripts, expected outputs, and required dashboard queries used by Security reviewer
All acceptance tests are executed in a customer-mirroring environment and results recorded in the onboarding checklist with attached artifacts (PRs, logs, screenshots)
signoff_checklist: Documentation: Confluence playbook linked and readable by external auditors (link in evidence_links)
API: Rotation endpoint documented in OpenAPI spec and covered by integration tests (PR link)
Observability: Audit events show required schema and are present in at least two sinks (internal SIEM + customer bucket)
Security: Threat model and risk delta reviewed and approved by Security (reviewer signature required)
Operator Controls: Break-glass policies configured with 2-of-3 approvers and TTL enforcement verified
Customer UX: Customer console shows rotation status, last-rotation timestamp, and required action items post-rotation
Recovery: Rollback runbook executed in a dry-run and post-rollback checks confirm data integrity
Legal/Compliance: Retention and exportability of audit evidence confirmed for customer's regulatory regime
Signoff: Product Manager, Security Lead, Ops Manager, and Customer Success each provide explicit signoff entries

2025-11-08 - Engineering spike completed: validated KV cache invalidation approach for seamless rotation (notes in GH issue #15812).

qa_test_matrix: Test A: API acceptance - submit signed rotation request -> expect 202 Accepted + correlation_id; confirm audit event present
Test B: KV cache invalidation - active session tokens rotated within window, no unauthorized token reuse observed
Test C: Operator break-glass - initiate emergency access with two approvers -> ephemeral creds issued with 15m TTL; verify automatic revocation
Test D: Rollback - simulate failure during re-encryption -> execute rollback steps and verify data integrity checksums match
Test E: Audit sink delivery - logs delivered to both internal SIEM and customer S3 within 5 minutes
notes: Risk: HSM vendor firmware older than v3.4 causes delayed rekey operations; vendor coordination required for specific customers.

Tradeoff: Shorter TTL on ephemeral operator creds reduces blast radius but increases operational friction for urgent fixes; currently set to 15 minutes with ability to extend via an auditable approval.
Follow-up: Add automated smoke test to onboarding job that verifies audit sink reachability prior to enabling customer-initiated rotations (new ticket to be created).
